meta.triageRationale: One cohesive change confined to the workflow define phase with a single obvious approach: extend the define runner's epic.frame + stories.compose step prompts/schemas to elicit functionalDefinition, and extend defineSynthesizer's body schema (orchestrator.ts:937, currently additionalProperties:false) to admit + carry it, plus define checklist.verify FR items. It reuses S001's already-shipped seams (functionalDefinition body field, mintFrId/parseFrId/isFrId, renderFunctionalRequirementsSection, functional-coverage dimension) — no new subsystem, no new contract. It is NOT trivial because it crosses the defineSynthesizer body-schema boundary (a validated ajv gate) and must stay absent-safe/backward-compatible, which warrants a design.story + tasks. Grounding is from direct reads this session (runners/define/index.ts, orchestrator.ts:879-960, artifacts/functional-definition.ts) since the request is a precise, pre-scoped wiring change.

api.name: mintFrId
api.signature: mintFrId(epicHash: string, createdAtISO: string, ordinal: number, storyId?: string): string

parameters.name: epicHash
parameters.purpose: The Epic hash the FR belongs to (from the artifact meta).

parameters.name: createdAtISO
parameters.purpose: The artifact createdAt timestamp, for the id's date component.

parameters.name: ordinal
parameters.purpose: The sequence number assigned in deterministic order (doc-level first, then per-story in story order).

parameters.name: storyId
parameters.purpose: For a per-item FR, the owning story id; omitted for doc-level FRs.

returns.meaning: A stable canonical FR id (E<date><hash8>[:S<nnn>]:FR<nnn>). CONSUMED UNCHANGED from src/workflow/id.ts — the synthesizer calls it to assign ids off the model.

postconditions: Same (epicHash, createdAt, ordinal, storyId) yields the same id — stable across regenerations given a fixed ordinal order.

errorCases.scenario: FR statements are elicited but the defineSynthesizer body schema was not extended to admit functionalDefinition — additionalProperties:false rejects the field.
errorCases.detection: The synthesize-turn ajv validation fails the DEF body because functionalDefinition is not a declared property; the whole synthesize errors.
errorCases.response: This story extends the body schema IN LOCKSTEP with the step-schema + assembly additions, so the field is admitted; a schema/assembly drift is caught by the define synthesize-path tests.
errorCases.userImpact: Without lockstep the define run hard-fails or silently drops FRs; with it, the assembled functionalDefinition flows into the DEF body.

errorCases.scenario: The assembled functionalDefinition is invalid (duplicate id, malformed id, or a per-story FR whose itemRef resolves to no story id).
errorCases.detection: defineSynthesizer runs validateFunctionalDefinition(fd, knownItemIds = story ids) after minting and gets a non-null error string.
errorCases.response: Fail the synthesize with the validator's message. Because ids are minted deterministically off mintFrId, dup/malformed ids indicate an assembly bug (not model output) — caught by assembly unit tests before ship.
errorCases.userImpact: A malformed FR set never reaches disk; the failure names the offending FR.

errorCases.scenario: The model, prompted for FR statements, instead emits implementation detail or restates the problem verbatim (low-quality FRs).
errorCases.detection: The checklist.verify FR items (fr2 outcome-worded, fr1 present-when-functional) flag it; a human sees the audit verdict at approval.
errorCases.response: Record the weak FRs as checklist misses / openQuestions rather than blocking synthesize; the reviewer decides. Content quality is advisory (soft items), not a hard-fail.
errorCases.userImpact: Weak FRs surface in the checklist for the reviewer instead of silently passing.

errorCases.scenario: An epicHash or createdAt needed for minting is missing/blank in the intent at assembly time.
errorCases.detection: defineSynthesizer reads intent/meta before minting; a missing epicHash or createdAt is detected there (mintFrId needs both).
errorCases.response: Skip FR assembly and omit functionalDefinition (absent-safe) rather than minting a malformed id; log a warning. The DEF still writes with an empty FR section.
errorCases.userImpact: A run lacking mint inputs degrades to no-FRs instead of failing or producing malformed ids.

edgeCases.input: A define run whose ask has no functional content (neither epic.frame nor stories.compose emits functionalRequirements).
edgeCases.expected: functionalDefinition is omitted entirely; renderFunctionalRequirementsSection returns [] and the FR section renders empty — identical to today's output (absent-safe, byte-compatible for no-FR DEFs).

edgeCases.input: Only doc-level FRs elicited (no per-story), or only per-story FRs (no doc-level).
edgeCases.expected: The synthesizer assembles whichever were elicited; mintFrId is called with storyId only for per-item FRs; the record validates and the renderer groups accordingly (doc-level list then per-item groups, empty groups omitted).

edgeCases.input: The EXTEND branch of define (scope.assess decided extend; acknowledged:true; no s2/s3).
edgeCases.expected: No FR assembly runs (there is no epic.frame/stories.compose on the extend path); functionalDefinition is absent; the extend artifact is unaffected.

edgeCases.input: Two FR statements with identical text under the same story.
edgeCases.expected: Each still gets a distinct minted id (ordinal differs), so validateFunctionalDefinition does not flag a dup id; the duplication is a content nit the checklist may note, not an error.

Because ordinals are assigned in a fixed order (doc-level first, then per-story in story order), FR ids shift only if the story order changes — a known, documented consequence of sequence-numbering; ids are stable when the story order is stable.

Per the s1 code bundle on the shipped FR seams.

The define body schema stays additionalProperties:false and functionalDefinition is OPTIONAL — existing DEFs without FRs still validate and render exactly as before (absent-safe); the change is forward-only and rewrites nothing on disk. migration.stateBefore: Per the s1 code bundle: the define runner's epic.frame + stories.compose steps (runners/define/index.ts + schemas.ts) elicit no functional requirements, and defineSynthesizer's body schema (orchestrator.ts:937) requires exactly flavor/problem/nonGoals/assumptions/constraints/stories/openQuestions under additionalProperties:false — so even if FRs were elicited they'd be rejected at synthesize. S001's functionalDefinition field, mintFrId, validateFunctionalDefinition, renderFunctionalRequirementsSection, and the functional-coverage dimension all exist but are inert: the DEF FR section renders empty on every real run.
migration.stateAfter: epic.frame elicits doc-level FR statements and stories.compose elicits per-story FR statements (both optional, additionalProperties:false retained); defineSynthesizer assembles a FunctionalDefinition by minting stable ids via mintFrId in a fixed order (doc-level first, then per-story in story order), setting scope/itemRef from the elicitation site, validating via validateFunctionalDefinition, and including functionalDefinition in the body only when non-empty; the define checklist.verify gains FR audit items. DEFs with functional content now render a populated Functional requirements section; DEFs without render exactly as before. Forward-only; nothing on disk rewritten.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional functionalRequirements array to epicFrameSchema and storiesComposeSchema (per-story), keeping additionalProperties:false — additive, no behavior change until the synthesizer reads them.
Extend the epic.frame + stories.compose prompts to ask for doc-level / per-story functional requirements in outcome terms (no ids).

Add optional functionalDefinition to the defineSynthesizer body schema (additionalProperties:false retained) and add the assembly HARD-RULE: mint ids via mintFrId in fixed order, set scope/itemRef, validate via validateFunctionalDefinition, include only when non-empty; skip on the EXTEND branch. Land with the assembly + synthesize-path unit tests in the same step.
Add the fr1/fr2/fr3 audit items to the define checklist.verify prompt (soft items, existing defineChecklistSchema shape — no schema change).
Add the integration test proving a full define synthesize writes body.functionalDefinition + a populated rendered FR section, and a no-FR run stays byte-compatible-empty.

migration.backwardCompat: All three schema touches (epicFrameSchema, storiesComposeSchema, defineSynthesizer body) add only OPTIONAL fields and retain additionalProperties:false, so existing define runs that omit functionalRequirements/functionalDefinition still validate. functionalDefinition is optional on the DEF body and renderFunctionalRequirementsSection is already []-safe, so existing DEFs on disk stay valid and render unchanged (empty FR section) — forward-only, no rewrite. defineSynthesizer keeps its signature; only its internal assembly + schema grow. The consumed S001 files (functional-definition.ts, id.ts) are not modified. The one visible change is intentional: DEFs authored WITH functional content now render a populated FR section where before it was always empty.

alternativesConsidered.name: Elicit FR statements in the steps; mint stable ids in the synthesizer
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: epic.frame elicits doc-level FR statements and stories.compose elicits per-story FR statements (no ids); defineSynthesizer mints stable FR ids via mintFrId, assembles + validates the functionalDefinition, and admits it to the body schema.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extend epicFrameSchema with an optional `functionalRequirements: [{ statement, rationale? }]` (doc-level) and its prompt to ask for the epic's functional requirements in outcome terms. Extend storiesComposeSchema so each story carries an optional `functionalRequirements: [{ statement, rationale? }]` and its prompt to ask for that story's FRs. Neither step emits ids or scope — scope is implied by WHERE the FR was elicited (epic.frame => 'doc'; per-story => 'item' with itemRef = story id). defineSynthesizer then assembles a single FunctionalDefinition: it mints each id with mintFrId(epicHash, createdAt, ordinal, storyId?) in a deterministic order, sets scope + itemRef, runs validateFunctionalDefinition(knownItemIds = story ids), and includes functionalDefinition in the body (schema extended, additionalProperties:false retained). checklist.verify gains FR audit items.
pros: Ids are minted deterministically off the model via the existing mintFrId — stable + sequence-numbered as S001 intended; the model never invents an id.
Scope/itemRef are inferred from elicitation site, so the model can't produce a dangling itemRef.
Consumes S001's functional-definition.ts + id.ts unchanged; the renderer already handles the assembled record.
Doc-level AND per-story FRs are both captured, matching FunctionalRequirement's scope union.
cons: The synthesizer gains real assembly logic (mint + scope + validate), not just verbatim carry — a bit more code + tests than a pure passthrough.
Ordinal assignment order must be defined + stable (doc-level first, then per-story in story order) so ids don't churn across regenerations.

alternativesConsidered.name: Elicit full FR objects (with ids) in the steps; synthesizer carries verbatim
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The steps emit complete FunctionalRequirement objects (id, statement, scope, itemRef) and the synthesizer copies them verbatim into functionalDefinition.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extend the step schemas to require full FunctionalRequirement objects including the id, and have the model emit ids directly (e.g. following the FR-id shape). defineSynthesizer copies the union verbatim and validates.
pros: Synthesizer stays a near-passthrough (minimal assembly logic).
One place (the step) holds the whole FR object.
cons: The MODEL invents ids — fragile: collisions, non-sequential, unstable across regenerations, and easy to malform against isFrId; defeats S001's stable-id guarantee.
Requires the model to know the epicHash + ordinal scheme to mint a correct id — leaking the id scheme into the prompt.
validateFunctionalDefinition would frequently reject model output (dup/malformed ids), making define runs brittle.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Near-passthrough synthesizer but the model invents ids — unstable, collision-prone, leaks the id scheme, and repeatedly fails validateFunctionalDefinition.

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-story FRs only; no doc-level elicitation
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Only stories.compose elicits per-story FR statements; there is no doc-level FR elicitation at epic.frame.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extend only storiesComposeSchema + its prompt to elicit per-story FR statements; defineSynthesizer mints ids (scope 'item') and assembles. epic.frame is left unchanged, so DEFs carry no document-level functional requirements.
pros: Smallest change — one step + the synthesizer.
Covers the common case (FRs bound to a story).
cons: Drops doc-level FRs entirely — but FunctionalRequirement.scope explicitly supports 'doc' and the DEF template's Summary is meant to foreground doc-level functional outcomes (S002), so this under-delivers the record S001 designed.
An epic-wide functional requirement not owned by a single story has nowhere to live.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Smallest change and correct for per-story FRs, but drops doc-level FRs which the record + S002 Summary need.
